I've been working this land for 50 years. My back isn't what it used to be, and it's just me and my wife now. We hire machines for the heavy work — plowing, seeding, harvesting. That's normal here in Quzhou now. I don't change what works.

**Wheat (plant October, harvest June):**
The full 24 mu goes to wheat first. I'll use the improved variety from the county seed station — I stopped saving my own seed about 15 years ago because the station variety outyields it. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest, then I apply base fertilizer before sowing: urea and diammonium phosphate, a little potash. I irrigate right after sowing to get emergence, again at jointing in April, and once more at heading. That's three waterings — less than I used to do, the well is getting harder to pump. Two pesticide passes: one herbicide in early spring, one fungicide spray if there's powdery mildew around heading. My neighbors do the same. I expect around 450 jin per mu — sorry, 450 kg.

**Maize (plant June, harvest September):**
Right after wheat comes off, I plant maize on the same 24 mu. I use hybrid seed — everyone does for maize now, the yield difference is too big to ignore. I do rotary tillage to break up the wheat stubble. I apply phosphorus and potash as base, then topdress nitrogen twice — at jointing and at tasseling. Two irrigations: one at emergence if it's dry, one at tasseling. Two pesticide applications: herbicide early, then check for corn borer. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

Two crops, same land, every year. That's what I know.
